Reduce excessive tiering so the silhouette reads as a strong continuous section.
Tighten setbacks to avoid a code-minimum staircase effect.
Increase public void legibility by centering the primary figure around a clearer courtyard.
Enlarge the court enough to be read as usable public space.
Orient the court opening toward the access edge to strengthen the public threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the stepped portion into a more continuous envelope so the section reads as a single inhabited landform rather than repetitive tiers.
Reduce the number of step events to keep the dominant gesture and avoid over-fragmenting the silhouette.
Soften the terraces so they read as a coherent public section rather than code-like stair steps.
Shift the primary figure toward a clearer carved void to produce a legible public court connected to the access edge.
Make the void proportion stronger so the court is architecturally decisive in plan.
Align the connector/opening logic to the verified access side in the program frame so the ground response faces the street edge.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact stepped block with a small roof terrace, but across the four views it does not fully cohere as a single spatial idea. The stepped upper mass is legible, yet it behaves more like layered stacking than an integrated neighborhood section. The main failure for this program is the weak public threshold: the thick blue access edge is not met by a convincing court, notch, undercut, or entry seam, so the ground response feels sealed and semantically opposite to the required active street edge. The parcel relation is acceptable but not especially resolved; the mass sits inside the green boundary without generating a dominant gesture that clearly organizes usable open space. Compared with the similar references, it borrows their stepped/courtyard language only loosely and misses the stronger void-centered or bridged civic section logic. Programmatically, it could become neighborhood-living, but in its present form the section and access relationship are too generic and too box-like to hard-pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and horizontally spread than the candidate; reference is calmer and more clearly void-centered.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part composition with a legible central void and upper-level bridge/connector creating public threshold complexity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Contains multiple volumes and a larger ensemble logic; not a direct match for a single compact mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a courtyard can support neighborhood program when the void remains civic and readable.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise mass with a central atrium/courtyard and folded roof can create active ground and clear public center.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is much more continuous and site-responsive; candidate’s steps read more like stacked volumes than one flowing landform.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, ribbon-like section can produce inhabitable topography and stepped public circulation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference has clearer multi-wing porosity and a stronger carved center than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a pronounced courtyard and setback upper masses can support mixed-use neighborhood character.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied, but the mass does not strongly translate the parcel into an active spatial figure.
Blue frontage/access edge is not answered by a legible public void or entry threshold.
The stepped silhouette is coherent, but the section reads as stacked massing rather than inhabitable public topography.
Dominant gesture is present only moderately; support and primary mass are not yet clearly differentiated at the ground.
